item.title: Eddie Vedder Pays Tribute to Glen Hansard By Busking at Late Singer’s Old Grafton Street Spot in Dublin
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to this special episode, where we're remembering the life and legacy of Glen Hansard, the talented Irish musician who passed away last week. After attending Hansard's funeral in Dublin, Pearl Jam's Eddie Vedder paid a heartfelt tribute to his friend and fellow musician.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Vedder took to the streets of Dublin, specifically Grafton Street, where Hansard got his start as a 13-year-old street performer. With the help of some local musicians, Vedder sang Pearl Jam's "Black" and Bruce Springsteen's "Drive All Night" on guitar. The impromptu performance was captured by Scottish musician Murdo Mitchell, who shared it on Instagram.
[Clip of Vedder singing "Black" plays briefly]
Host: According to Mitchell, the performance was a spontaneous gathering of friends, with Vedder asking if they'd be up for a busk on Grafton Street after the funeral. They rallied a group of friends and headed down to the street, even though it was 3 am. As Mitchell said, "His spirit was there. Not got much footage of it. We only had my guitar, a broken string & some heart, but we made it work."
[Clip of Vedder singing "Drive All Night" plays briefly]
Host: This touching tribute is a testament to the deep bond between Vedder and Hansard, who met in 2010 after a traumatic event during a Swell Season show. Vedder had reached out to Hansard, offering support and kindness, and the two became friends. Hansard had spoken about the impact of Vedder's compassion, saying it was a turning point for him during a difficult time.
[Soft music continues to play]
Host: Hansard's funeral was a celebration of his life, with tributes from fellow musicians, including Bono, who shared a reworked version of U2's "Beautiful Day". The service was a testament to the love and admiration Hansard inspired among his peers.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today's episode. We hope you've enjoyed this special tribute to Glen Hansard. Eddie Vedder's impromptu performance on Grafton Street is a reminder of the power of music to bring people together and celebrate the lives of those who inspire us.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
